Train staff on the cryptographic policy and the importance of using cryptographic controls effectively.
Implement technical solutions to enforce the cryptographic policy across relevant systems and applications.
Regularly review and update the cryptographic policy to ensure it remains effective against emerging threats.

controls.name: key management
controls.description: A policy on the use, protection and lifetime of cryptographic keys shall be developed and implemented through their whole lifecycle.

deployment_points.name: Develop a comprehensive key management policy that outlines the procedures for key generation, distribution, storage, and destruction.
Implement a secure key storage solution, such as a hardware security module (HSM), to protect cryptographic keys from unauthorized access.
Establish a key lifecycle management process that includes regular audits and reviews of key usage and access logs.
Train personnel on key management best practices and the importance of safeguarding cryptographic keys throughout their lifecycle.
Regularly update the key management policy to reflect changes in technology, threats, and organizational requirements.

controls.name: physical security perimeter
controls.description: Security perimeters shall be defined and used to protect areas that contain either sensitive or critical information and information processing facilities.

deployment_points.name: Identify and map out all areas containing sensitive or critical information and establish clear security perimeters around these areas.
Install physical barriers such as fences, walls, or gates to delineate the security perimeter and restrict unauthorized access.
Implement surveillance systems, such as CCTV cameras, to monitor the security perimeter and detect any unauthorized access attempts.
Establish access control measures, including security personnel and identification checks, to ensure only authorized individuals can enter the perimeter.
Regularly review and update the security perimeter to address any changes in the environment or security threats.

controls.name: physical entry controls
controls.description: Secure areas shall be protected by appropriate entry controls to ensure that only authorized personnel are allowed access.

deployment_points.name: Implement access control systems, such as key cards or biometric scanners, to restrict entry to secure areas.
Maintain a list of authorized personnel who are permitted access to secure areas and regularly update this list.
Train security personnel on entry control procedures and the importance of verifying identities before granting access.
Conduct regular audits of access logs to identify any unauthorized access attempts and take corrective actions as necessary.
Establish a visitor management system to track and control access for temporary visitors to secure areas.

controls.name: securing offices, rooms and facilities
controls.description: Physical security for offices, rooms and facilities shall be designed and applied.

deployment_points.name: Conduct a risk assessment to identify vulnerabilities in offices, rooms, and facilities that require physical security measures.
Install locks, security doors, and window bars to enhance physical security in vulnerable areas.
Implement an alarm system to detect unauthorized access or breaches in security within offices and facilities.
Regularly inspect and maintain physical security measures to ensure they are functioning effectively and address any weaknesses.
Develop and communicate emergency response plans for incidents related to physical security breaches.

controls.name: protecting against external and environmental threats
controls.description: Physical protection against natural disasters, malicious attack or accidents shall be designed and applied.

deployment_points.name: Conduct a risk assessment to identify potential external and environmental threats to the organization, such as floods, fires, or vandalism.
Implement physical barriers, such as flood walls or fire-resistant materials, to protect against identified threats.
Develop and maintain an emergency response plan that includes procedures for responding to external threats and environmental disasters.
Regularly train staff on emergency procedures and conduct drills to ensure preparedness for potential incidents.
Review and update protection measures regularly to adapt to changing environmental conditions and threat landscapes.

controls.name: working in secure areas
controls.description: Procedures for working in secure areas shall be designed and applied.

deployment_points.name: Develop clear procedures for working in secure areas, including access protocols and safety measures.
Train employees on the specific requirements and responsibilities associated with working in secure areas.
Implement monitoring systems to ensure compliance with established procedures while working in secure areas.
Conduct regular reviews and audits of procedures to identify areas for improvement and ensure effectiveness.
Establish a reporting mechanism for employees to report any security incidents or breaches while working in secure areas.

controls.name: delivery and loading areas
controls.description: Access points such as delivery and loading areas and other points where unauthorized persons could enter the premises shall be controlled and, if possible, isolated from information processing facilities to avoid unauthorized access.

deployment_points.name: Designate specific delivery and loading areas that are separate from sensitive information processing facilities.
Implement access control measures, such as gates and security personnel, to monitor and restrict access to delivery and loading areas.
Train staff on procedures for receiving deliveries and managing access to these areas to prevent unauthorized entry.
Install surveillance cameras to monitor activity in delivery and loading areas and deter unauthorized access.
Regularly review and update access control measures to ensure they remain effective against potential threats.

controls.name: equipment siting and protection
controls.description: Equipment shall be sited and protected to reduce the risks from environmental threats and hazards, and opportunities for unauthorized access.

deployment_points.name: Conduct a site assessment to determine the best locations for equipment that minimize exposure to environmental threats.
Install protective measures, such as enclosures or climate control systems, to safeguard equipment from environmental hazards.
Implement access controls to restrict unauthorized personnel from accessing equipment areas.
Regularly inspect and maintain equipment and protective measures to ensure they are functioning properly.
Develop a contingency plan for equipment failure or damage due to environmental threats.

controls.name: supporting utilities
controls.description: Equipment shall be protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.

deployment_points.name: Install uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) to provide backup power to critical equipment during outages.
Regularly test and maintain UPS systems to ensure they are operational when needed.
Implement redundancy for critical utilities, such as backup generators, to minimize the impact of utility failures.
Monitor utility performance and establish alerts for any disruptions to proactively address issues.
Develop a response plan for utility failures that includes communication protocols and recovery procedures.

controls.name: cabling security
controls.description: Power and telecommunications cabling carrying data or supporting information services shall be protected from interception, interference or damage.

deployment_points.name: Route cabling through secure pathways that are inaccessible to unauthorized personnel to prevent tampering.
Use protective conduits or shielding for cabling to guard against physical damage and interception.
Regularly inspect cabling for signs of wear, damage, or unauthorized access attempts.
Implement monitoring systems to detect any interference or breaches in cabling security.
Develop and enforce policies for the installation and maintenance of cabling to ensure compliance with security standards.

controls.name: equipment maintenance
controls.description: Equipment shall be correctly maintained to ensure its continued availability and integrity.

deployment_points.name: Establish a maintenance schedule for all equipment, detailing frequency and types of maintenance required.
Assign qualified personnel to perform maintenance tasks and ensure they are trained on the specific equipment.
Document all maintenance activities, including dates, actions taken, and any issues identified during maintenance.
Implement a tracking system to monitor equipment performance and maintenance history to identify trends or recurring issues.
Review and update maintenance procedures regularly to incorporate new best practices and address any identified gaps.

controls.name: removal of assets
controls.description: Equipment, information or software shall not be taken off-site without prior authorization.

deployment_points.name: Develop a formal policy outlining the process for requesting authorization to remove assets from the premises.
Create a standardized asset removal request form that includes details such as the asset type, purpose of removal, and duration.
Designate specific personnel responsible for reviewing and approving asset removal requests.
Maintain a log of all approved and denied requests to ensure accountability and traceability.
Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with the asset removal policy and address any unauthorized removals.

controls.name: security of equipment and assets off-premises
controls.description: Security shall be applied to off-site assets taking into account the different risks of working outside the organizationΓÇÖs premises.

deployment_points.name: Assess the risks associated with off-site work and develop security measures tailored to those risks.
Provide training to employees on secure handling and storage of equipment and assets when off-premises.
Implement encryption and password protection for sensitive data stored on portable devices taken off-site.
Establish a protocol for reporting lost or stolen equipment and ensure employees are aware of this process.
Regularly review and update security measures for off-site assets based on emerging threats and incidents.

controls.name: secure disposal or reuse of equipment
controls.description: All items of equipment containing storage media shall be verified to ensure that any sensitive data and licensed software has been removed or securely overwritten prior to disposal or re-use.

deployment_points.name: Develop a secure disposal policy that outlines procedures for handling equipment containing storage media.
Use certified data destruction methods to ensure all sensitive data is irretrievable before disposal or reuse.
Maintain records of all disposed or reused equipment, including the method of data destruction used.
Train staff on the importance of secure disposal and the specific procedures to follow.
Conduct periodic audits to verify compliance with the secure disposal policy and identify any areas for improvement.

controls.name: unattended user equipment
controls.description: Users shall ensure that unattended equipment has appropriate protection.

deployment_points.name: Implement a policy requiring users to lock their devices when leaving them unattended, regardless of duration.
Provide training to users on the importance of securing unattended equipment and the potential risks of neglect.
Utilize automatic screen lock features on devices to minimize exposure when not in use.
Conduct regular awareness campaigns to reinforce the importance of securing unattended equipment.
Monitor compliance with the policy and address any violations through appropriate disciplinary measures.

controls.name: clear desk and clear screen policy
controls.description: A clear desk policy for papers and removable storage media and a clear screen policy for information processing facilities shall be adopted.

deployment_points.name: Develop and communicate a clear desk and clear screen policy to all employees, outlining expectations and responsibilities.
Provide secure storage options for sensitive documents and removable media to facilitate compliance with the policy.
Conduct regular training sessions to educate employees on the importance of maintaining a clear desk and screen.
Implement periodic inspections to ensure adherence to the policy and provide feedback to employees.
Establish consequences for non-compliance to reinforce the importance of the policy.

controls.name: documented operating procedures
controls.description: Operating procedures shall be documented and made available to all users who need them.

deployment_points.name: Identify all critical processes and procedures that require documentation for user reference.
Create clear, concise, and accessible documentation for each identified procedure, ensuring it is easy to understand.
Implement a centralized repository where all documented procedures can be stored and accessed by users.
Regularly review and update documentation to reflect changes in processes or organizational structure.
Train users on how to access and utilize the documented procedures effectively.

controls.name: change management
controls.description: Changes to the organization, business processes, information processing facilities and systems that affect information security shall be controlled.

deployment_points.name: Establish a formal change management process that includes request, assessment, approval, and implementation stages.
Designate a change advisory board to review and approve significant changes affecting information security.
Document all changes, including the rationale, impact assessment, and approval records.
Conduct post-implementation reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of changes and identify any issues.
Provide training to staff on the change management process to ensure compliance and understanding.

controls.name: capacity management
controls.description: The use of resources shall be monitored, tuned and projections made of future capacity requirements to ensure the required system performance.

deployment_points.name: Implement monitoring tools to track resource usage and performance metrics across systems and applications.
Analyze historical data to identify trends in resource consumption and predict future capacity needs.
Establish thresholds for resource usage that trigger alerts for potential capacity issues.
Regularly review and adjust resource allocation based on performance data and projected growth.
Document capacity management processes and ensure they are communicated to relevant stakeholders.

controls.name: separation of development, testing and operational environments
controls.description: Development, testing, and operational environments shall be separated to reduce the risks of unauthorized access or changes to the operational environment.

deployment_points.name: Establish distinct environments for development, testing, and production to prevent cross-contamination.
Implement access controls to restrict personnel from moving between environments without proper authorization.
Document the processes for promoting code and changes from development to testing and then to production.
Regularly review and audit the separation of environments to ensure compliance with established policies.
Provide training to staff on the importance of maintaining separation and the risks associated with non-compliance.

controls.name: controls against malware
controls.description: Detection, prevention and recovery controls to protect against malware shall be implemented, combined with appropriate user awareness.

deployment_points.name: Implement antivirus and anti-malware solutions on all endpoints and servers to detect and prevent malware infections.
Schedule regular updates for malware definitions and software to ensure protection against the latest threats.
Conduct user training sessions to raise awareness about malware threats and safe computing practices.
Establish a response plan for malware incidents, including isolation of infected systems and recovery procedures.
Regularly review and test the effectiveness of malware controls and user awareness programs.

controls.name: information backup
controls.description: Backup copies of information, software and system images shall be taken and tested regularly in accordance with an agreed backup policy.

deployment_points.name: Develop a comprehensive backup policy that outlines the frequency, scope, and methods of backups for all critical data.
Implement automated backup solutions to ensure regular and consistent backups of information and system images.
Store backup copies in a secure, offsite location to protect against data loss from physical disasters.
Regularly test backup restoration processes to ensure data can be recovered quickly and accurately when needed.
Review and update the backup policy periodically to adapt to changes in data volume and organizational needs.

controls.name: event logging
controls.description: Event logs recording user activities, exceptions, faults and information security events shall be produced, kept and regularly reviewed.

deployment_points.name: Configure systems to generate logs for user activities, security events, and system errors to ensure comprehensive event tracking.
Establish a centralized logging system to collect and store logs from various sources for easier management and analysis.
Define log retention policies to determine how long logs should be kept based on compliance and operational needs.
Implement regular reviews of logs to identify anomalies or security incidents that require further investigation.
Ensure that logging mechanisms are protected against tampering and unauthorized access to maintain the integrity of log data.

controls.name: protection of log information
controls.description: Logging facilities and log information shall be protected against tampering and unauthorized access.

deployment_points.name: Implement access controls to restrict who can view and modify log files, ensuring only authorized personnel have access.
Use encryption to protect log data both in transit and at rest to prevent unauthorized access and tampering.
Regularly audit access to log files to detect any unauthorized attempts to access or alter log information.
Establish a secure logging infrastructure that includes redundancy and backup to prevent data loss.
Train staff on the importance of log protection and the procedures for reporting any suspicious activities related to log access.

controls.name: administrator and operator logs
controls.description: System administrator and system operator activities shall be logged and the logs protected and regularly reviewed.

deployment_points.name: Enable detailed logging for all administrative and operational activities on critical systems to ensure accountability.
Store administrator and operator logs in a secure location separate from the systems being monitored to prevent tampering.
Conduct regular reviews of these logs to identify any unauthorized or suspicious activities performed by administrators or operators.
Implement alerts for specific actions taken by administrators that may indicate potential security breaches or policy violations.
Provide training for administrators and operators on the importance of logging and the procedures for maintaining log integrity.

controls.name: clock synchronisation
controls.description: The clocks of all relevant information processing systems within an organization or security domain shall be synchronised to a single reference time source.

deployment_points.name: Select a reliable time source, such as an NTP server, to synchronize all relevant information processing systems.
Configure all systems to automatically synchronize their clocks with the chosen time source at regular intervals.
Monitor synchronization status to ensure all systems maintain accurate time and address any discrepancies promptly.
Document the synchronization process and any configurations made to ensure consistency across the organization.
Regularly review and test the synchronization setup to ensure it remains effective and compliant with organizational policies.

controls.name: installation of software on operational systems
controls.description: Procedures shall be implemented to control the installation of software on operational systems.

deployment_points.name: Develop and document a formal procedure for software installation that includes approval processes and testing requirements.
Restrict software installation privileges to authorized personnel only, ensuring that users cannot install unauthorized applications.
Implement a software inventory management system to track installed applications and their versions across all operational systems.
Regularly review installed software to ensure compliance with organizational policies and remove any unauthorized applications.
Provide training for staff on the software installation procedures and the importance of adhering to these controls.

controls.name: management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.description: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems being used shall be obtained in a timely fashion, the organizationΓÇÖs exposure to such vulnerabilities evaluated and appropriate measures taken to address the associated risk.

Conduct regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing to identify and evaluate the organization's exposure to risks.
Develop a remediation plan for addressing identified vulnerabilities, prioritizing based on risk and potential impact.
Document and communicate the status of vulnerabilities and remediation efforts to relevant stakeholders to ensure transparency.

controls.name: restrictions on software installation
controls.description: Rules governing the installation of software by users shall be established and implemented.

deployment_points.name: Create a formal policy that outlines the rules and procedures for software installation by users, including approval processes.
Implement technical controls to enforce the policy, such as application whitelisting or software restriction policies.
Train users on the software installation policy and the risks associated with unauthorized software installations.
Regularly review and update the policy to reflect changes in technology and organizational needs.
Monitor compliance with the policy and take corrective actions for any violations to maintain security.

controls.name: information systems audit controls
controls.description: Audit requirements and activities involving verification of operational systems shall be carefully planned and agreed to minimise disruptions to business processes.

deployment_points.name: Develop an audit plan that outlines the scope, objectives, and schedule for auditing operational systems.
Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to ensure that audit activities are planned to minimize disruptions to business operations.
Use automated tools to assist in the auditing process, ensuring efficiency and accuracy in data collection.
Document audit findings and recommendations clearly, providing actionable insights for system improvements.
Conduct follow-up reviews to ensure that audit recommendations are implemented effectively and to assess their impact on operations.

controls.name: network controls
controls.description: Networks shall be managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.

deployment_points.name: Establish a network management policy that outlines the roles and responsibilities for network security management.
Implement firewalls and intrusion detection systems to monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic.
Regularly update network devices and software to protect against vulnerabilities and ensure compliance with security standards.
Conduct periodic network assessments and audits to identify and mitigate potential security risks.
Train staff on network security best practices and incident response procedures to enhance overall security awareness.

controls.name: security of network services
controls.description: Security mechanisms, service levels and management requirements of all network services shall be identified and included in network services agreements, whether these services are provided in-house or outsourced.

deployment_points.name: Define security requirements for network services in a formal document that outlines expectations and responsibilities.
Include specific security mechanisms such as encryption and access controls in service level agreements (SLAs) with providers.
Regularly review and update network service agreements to reflect changes in security standards and organizational needs.
Conduct risk assessments for all network services to identify potential vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies.
Ensure that all personnel involved in managing network services are trained on security policies and procedures.

controls.name: segregation in networks
controls.description: Groups of information services, users and information systems shall be segregated on networks.

deployment_points.name: Identify and classify information services and systems based on sensitivity and criticality to determine segregation needs.
Implement VLANs (Virtual Local Area Networks) to separate different groups of users and services within the network.

Regularly review and update segregation policies to ensure they align with current organizational structure and security requirements.
Monitor network traffic between segregated segments to detect and respond to unauthorized access attempts.

controls.name: information transfer policies and procedures
controls.description: Formal transfer policies, procedures and controls shall be in place to protect the transfer of information through the use of all types of communication facilities.

deployment_points.name: Develop and document formal information transfer policies that outline acceptable methods and protocols for data transfer.
Implement encryption for all sensitive information being transferred to protect against unauthorized access.
Establish procedures for verifying the identity of recipients before transferring sensitive information.
Train employees on the importance of secure information transfer and the procedures to follow.
Regularly review and update transfer policies to address emerging threats and changes in technology.

controls.name: agreements on information transfer
controls.description: Agreements shall address the secure transfer of business information between the organization and external parties.

deployment_points.name: Draft formal agreements that specify security requirements for information transfer with external parties.
Include clauses that mandate the use of encryption and secure transfer protocols in all agreements.
Establish a process for regularly reviewing and updating agreements to ensure they remain relevant and effective.
Conduct due diligence on external parties to assess their security practices before entering into agreements.
Provide training to relevant staff on the importance of adhering to information transfer agreements.

controls.name: electronic messaging
controls.description: Information involved in electronic messaging shall be appropriately protected.

deployment_points.name: Implement encryption for all electronic messages containing sensitive information to protect against interception.
Establish policies that define acceptable use and security measures for electronic messaging systems.
